candidates.source_body_excerpt: ROCHDALE HORNETS coach Gary Thornton says Samy Kibula will provide not only the size and physical presence expected of a prop, but also a helpful amount of skill. The 27-year-old former Super League player who started out at Wigan Warriors has joined from Swinton Lions to become Hornets’ fifth close-season addition. Halfback Ben White from Batley Bulldogs is a high-profile recruit, while Rochdale aim to bring out the potential in threequarters Harry Ratcliffe (from Wakefield Trinity), Dylan Proud (Keighley Cougars) and Jack Twigg (Huddersfield Giants). Kibula, born in the Democratic Republic of the Congo before a family move to the UK, came through the Wigan system to make one appearance for the first team (in 2018). He has also played in the top flight for Warrington Wolves and Castleford Tigers, and outside it for Bradford Bulls and Batley (in two spells) as well as Swinton, where he spent this year, featuring 13 times. The 27-year-old has also had various loan stints, taking his total number of games to three figures, and having lost prop Jordan Andrade to retirement, Thornton will welcome that experience to his front row. “We are really pleased to have signed Samy, and I’d like to thank (chairman) Andy Mazey for getting this one over the line,” he said. “With Jordan not around, we needed to bring in an experienced middle-unit player, and Samy has a wealth of experience in the Championship and Super League which will be invaluable to our group.

candidates.source_body_excerpt: Community equipment services provider Medequip has been awarded the contract to deliver the Community Equipment Loan Service (CELS) for Oldham, Rochdale, Stockport and Tameside (ORST). The contract has been awarded by a partnership of four local authorities, comprising Oldham, Rochdale, Stockport and Tameside councils, together with the NHS Greater Manchester Integrated Care Board (ICB). Commencing on 1 October 2026, the contract will initially run for three years, with the option to extend for up to a further two years. The service plays a vital role in supporting adults and children to live independently and safely at home. Working closely with health and social care prescribers across the four boroughs, Medequip will provide the full lifecycle management of community equipment, including procurement, delivery, installation, maintenance, repair, collection, decontamination, refurbishment and recycling. Community equipment services are a key part of integrated health and social care systems, helping to facilitate timely hospital discharge, support reablement and recovery, prevent avoidable hospital admissions and enable people to remain independent in their own homes and communities for longer. As part of the mobilisation of the new contract, Medequip will initially operate from the existing service depot in Dukinfield, ensuring continuity of service for residents and prescribing professionals. Medequip will then relocate to a purpose-built, spacious 32,450 square feet service centre depot within the Hollinwood Junction development. The modern, energy-efficient building has been designed with sustainability in mind and benefits from excellent transport and motorway connections, supporting efficient service delivery across all four boroughs. The new location will provide enhanced operational capacity and support Medequip’s continued focus on delivering responsive, high-quality services while maximising the collection, refurbishment and reuse of equipment through sustainable circular economy principles.

A decade ago the American crossed the pond in a bid to restore what he believes to be his ancestral home. The local authority felt the US-born Middletonian had not made enough progress and ended the agreement. candidates.source_body_excerpt: This chilling workshop will look at horror fiction of the page and screen, questioning who and what belongs in the home. For many, the home is a physical location which – through its sturdy walls and locked doors – protects us from the dangers of the outside world. However, in the modern world, technology and devices can open new doors into our homes: the spectres of history and society can enter whether they are invited or not. During the workshop, we will put pen to paper and reclaim what the home means to us, exploring how horror can help us to confront and understand our anxieties in a creative way. The workshop will include discussions and guided writing activities. No previous writing experience is necessary, and there’s no pressure to share anything during the workshop. Bring something to write with or on if you like, but we will also have pens and paper. Events and activities are not organised by Rochdale Borough Council unless stated otherwise. candidates.source_body_excerpt: Four arrests were made as police seized drugs worth an estimated £1 million in a series of raids at dawn in Rochdale on Monday. Greater Manchester Police said the swoops followed a six month-long probe into a 'suspected large-scale supply and distribution of illicit drugs'. Detectives said they believe the operation was 'supplying drugs both online and in person to customers nationally'. Officers from GMP's Serious Organised Crime Group (SOCG), supported by the Tactical Aid Unit, executed six warrants across the town. The premises targeted, said police, were equipped with security measures. Click here to get the biggest stories straight to your inbox in our Daily Newsletter The force said it uncovered what is believed to be a 'dedicated drugs storage facility' on Manchester Road, Rochdale. A 'vast quantity' of suspected drugs were subsequently found inside, GMP added. Police said a list detailing more than 100 different types of drugs - ranging across Class A, B and C - were discovered, with a 'significant proportion' of the haul said to be prescription-type medication alongside bodybuilding and weight-loss drugs. A number of electronic devices were also seized, including more than 30 mobile phones, with an estimated £60,000 in cash recovered. Two men aged 52 and 23 were arrested on Twinegate, Rochdale, with a man aged 51 also arrested on Whittaker Lane, Rochdale. The fourth suspect, a man aged 44, was arrested on Kingsway. All four were held on suspicion of conspiracy to supply Class A, B and C drugs and remained in custody on Monday afternoon. Detective Inspector Rich McCorry, from GMP's Serious Organised Crime Group, said the investigation, codenamed 'Nostalgic', would continue. "Let this be a clear message to anyone choosing to involve themselves in serious and organised crime. Greater Manchester Police will not stand for it and we will find you. We will work relentlessly to disrupt the lifestyle your criminality is funding. "We believe this is a sophisticated and well-established organised crime group. The premises we entered today were fully equipped with security measures, laptops and large quantities of drugs, indicating what we suspect was a highly organised operation supplying drugs both online and in person to customers nationally. "This type of criminality fuels violence, exploitation and misery in our communities, while those responsible seek to profit from it. We are determined to dismantle these networks."

candidates.source_body_excerpt: Police have seized an estimated £1 million worth of drugs and arrested four people as part of an investigation into the suspected large-scale supply and distribution of illicit drugs. Officers from the Serious Organised Crime Group (SOCG), supported by the Tactical Aid Unit (TAU), executed six warrants across Rochdale this morning. Over the past six months, officers have worked to build a detailed intelligence picture, using surveillance, telecommunications data and a range of investigative enquiries to establish the scale of the suspected drugs network and identify those believed to be involved. That work led officers to several premises believed to be linked to the storage and distribution of illicit drugs on a significant commercial scale. During this morning’s warrants, officers uncovered what is suspected to be a dedicated drugs storage facility in Manchester Road, Rochdale. From the outside, the address appeared to be a residential property, but inside officers discovered vast quantities of suspected illicit drugs with an estimated value of more than £1 million. Officers also discovered a list detailing more than 100 different types of drugs believed to have been supplied by the organised crime group, ranging across Class A, B and C drugs. A significant proportion of the haul consisted of prescription-type medication, alongside bodybuilding and weight-loss drugs.

candidates.source_body_excerpt: Dr Helen Palmer has been appointed independent Chair of Rochdale Creates, the borough’s Cultural Compact. The partnership brings together organisations and individuals working in culture, education, business and the community. Dr Palmer has more than 30 years’ experience in culture, heritage, tourism and partnership development. She has previously worked with Touchstones Rochdale, Rochdale Borough Council and Rochdale Development Agency. As Chair, she will lead the partnership’s governance and help its members work together on cultural projects across the borough. Dr Palmer, who runs the consultancy Palmer Squared and is Co Chair of What Next? Greater Manchester, said: “Rochdale has developed an ambitious and compelling vision for culture, built on strong partnerships, rich heritage and a growing creative sector. I am excited to support Rochdale Creates as it enters its next phase and to work alongside partners across the borough to help turn that ambition into action.” Rochdale Creates was established in 2022. Its members include artists, cultural organisations, educators, businesses, community groups and public sector partners. Councillor Sue Smith, Rochdale Borough Council’s Cabinet Member for Communities and Cooperation, said: “We are delighted to welcome Helen as Chair of Rochdale Creates. This is a significant appointment for the borough's cultural sector and reflects how far the Cultural Compact has come since it was established three years ago. Attracting someone of Helen's calibre, profile and experience demonstrates the strength of Rochdale's cultural and creative sector and the exciting opportunities that exist here.”

candidates.source_body_excerpt: Rochdale Council has launched a “Stop Means Stop” campaign to remind drivers to stop for school crossing patrols. It says parking enforcement patrols outside schools will also increase. Councillor Dylan Williams, the council’s cabinet member for Highways and Facilities, launched the campaign at St Luke’s Primary School in Heywood. The council said it recorded 137 instances of drivers failing to stop outside schools over the past five years, including cases where a crossing patrol had already stepped into the road. “There have been multiple cases across the borough and across Greater Manchester with cars not stopping for the lollipop people,” Cllr Williams said. “This is obviously a real danger for schoolchildren across the borough. It’s really important that people stop.” The council is also asking drivers to keep yellow lines and school keep-clear markings free of parked vehicles. Cllr Williams said the increased parking patrols would take place without a fixed schedule. A crossing patrol worker at St Luke’s, identified as Chris, said vehicles parked on zigzag lines obstructed both his view and the view of passing drivers. candidates.source_body_excerpt: Councillor Lee Wolf has called for an urgent meeting with police and council officers over reports of disorder in Middleton town centre and at the former Durnford Street School site. In a post to a local Facebook group, Councillor Wolf said he was requesting a meeting of the Middleton Township Committee with Greater Manchester Police and senior council officers. “Our town cannot become a no-go zone for residents,” he wrote. “We need immediate action taken to disperse these groups and an increased police presence on our streets.” In a separate public post, he alleged that groups of young people were entering the former school site daily and climbing onto its roof. He said stones and mud had been thrown at passing and parked cars, and claimed that some parents had dropped children off at the site. Councillor Wolf said the building was not properly secured and criticised the property owners’ response. He said he was speaking to council officers about enforcement action and called for cameras at the site, including cameras capable of recording vehicle registration plates. He urged residents to report every incident to police so there would be an official record. People responding to his town centre post described further concerns. Tracey Kelly said she had nearly been hit by someone riding a bike while wearing a balaclava and alleged that fireworks had been directed towards shops and cars. Trisha Catherine said fireworks had been set off in bins outside a town centre business on a previous Saturday night. Michelle Jarvis described young people throwing fireworks and entering and leaving food shops near Tesco. Another commenter alleged that objects had been thrown at staff inside McDonald’s.

candidates.source_body_excerpt: A monthly group for neurodivergent people, families and carers in Prestwich is marking its first anniversary in September. Michelle Mackin, a care co-ordinator working with Bury GP Federation and local GP practices, set up Different Minds, One Community after seeing a need for a place where people could find advice and meet others. The group meets at The Woodthorpe on Bury Old Road. Michelle said it brings together support from social prescribing staff and community groups. Dominic Burke, who has experienced severe food anxiety for more than a decade, said attending the group had helped him find support for his health and search for work. “The group has given me somewhere to go and meet other people in smaller groups, know I will be supported, and get advice,” he said. He has also taken part in activities at Prestwich’s Creative Living Centre and received CV guidance. Maxine Ackerley, a parent of neurodivergent children, said meeting other parents and carers had helped her share experiences and find advice. “This group gives you somewhere to come and be heard and helped,” she said. Different Minds, One Community meets on the second Wednesday of each month from 1.30pm to 3pm at The Woodthorpe, Bury Old Road, Prestwich M25 0EG. candidates.source_body_excerpt: A campaign has been launched to keep children safe by reminding drivers they have to stop for school crossing patrols. The drive was launched last week at St Luke’s Primary School in Heywood. Cllr Dylan Williams launches the Stop Means Stop campaign at St Luke’s Primary School in Heywood. candidates.source_body_excerpt: Greater Manchester Police officers attended an address on Tweedale Street in Rochdale at approximately 4 p.m. on Monday, 25 May 2026, following reports of a concern for welfare. Officers discovering the 44-year-old woman deceased at the scene initiated immediate contact with ambulance services, though medical personnel could only confirm the victim’s death rather than undertake resuscitative measures. The initial incident classification reflected uncertainty regarding the cause of death, with responding officers treating the circumstances as potentially suspicious rather than immediately declaring murder investigation protocols. However, subsequent examination and preliminary forensic assessment rapidly escalated the investigation to full murder inquiry status. Detective senior investigating officers commenced immediate containment procedures, establishing crime scene security and preserving evidence for later forensic examination. Specialist teams from Greater Manchester Police’s Major Incident Team assumed investigative responsibilities, utilising established protocols for homicide inquiries. Kyle Howard, aged 25 years old and residing at the same Tweedale Street property where the victim was discovered, was arrested on suspicion of murder within hours of the police response. Howard’s presence at the address and circumstantial evidence established through immediate neighbourhood canvassing and witness interviews accelerated suspect identification significantly. By 3 June 2026, eight days following the initial discovery, Greater Manchester Police confirmed that Howard had been charged with murder and remanded in custody pending court proceedings. His appearance at Manchester Magistrates Court on 3 June 2026 formalised the charge, with the defendant remanded in custody pending further court appearances and trial preparation. Greater Manchester Police characterised the investigation as complete regarding the immediate arrest phase, though ongoing inquiries continued regarding potential additional circumstances or contributing factors surrounding the death. Greater Manchester Police’s Major Incident Team operates structured investigative frameworks encompassing witness identification, forensic evidence preservation, and secure evidence chain management. Following death notification to next of kin, supported by specialist family liaison officers, investigators establish timeline reconstructions, witness statement gathering, and preliminary forensic assessment protocols. Detective Chief Inspector Liz Hopkinson, of Greater Manchester Police’s Major Incident Team, told investigators that “this is a tragic set of circumstances where a woman has lost her life, and we have a team of dedicated officers working around the clock to establish what happened.” The characterisation reflects the emotional gravity of homicide investigations whilst emphasising systematic investigative commitment.

candidates.source_body_excerpt: Vale of Lune’s winning streak continued as they kicked off the new season with Saturday’s 32-28 victory at Rochdale, writes BARRY LEES. The first XV’s first meaningful encounter of the NW1 adventure had seen livewire flanker Sam Walton leave early for treatment to an eye injury. Reorganising ensued and the skill set of the crew on the bench began to kick in. Rochdale stepped up production and pressed into the Vale 22, where they powered over the tryline to open the scoring. They soon added a second to reinforce their intent as Alex Ryder came on to bolster Vale’s forward effort. From a sustained period of possession, Jordan Dorrington made the crucial break for Ben McGarvey to strike in the right corner. However, Mike Bradshaw infringed the rucking rules and was dispatched for a breather. It was time for Vale to dig deep and Eddie Abdelghafar led the backs’ charge, earning a chance for Jamie Mayall to slot over a penalty kick which left Vale six points behind the home team at the break, trailing 14-8. With Alex Briggs making a welcome return to first-team rugby after injury, a high clearance from the Vale fell to Rochdale’s nippy centre. They darted through the gaps to set up the next Rochdale try before more Vale changes saw Ben Gould come on for his debut in place of scrum-half Matty Kaye. A Rochdale foot in touch was flagged by the touch judge but overruled by the referee, with the resulting possession setting off a passing phase across the pitch for their fourth try of the afternoon. Sam Wallbank also transgressed the tackling laws, which meant he headed for the bench. With 17 points in it, a man down and 15 minutes remaining on the clock, it was no time for the faint-hearted. The Vale squad showed it is anything but that, starting with the flamboyant Jack Macfarlane pulling a try back and Mayall adding the garnish. Grafting together with increased energy, the Vale pack enabled prop Tadgh Butler to register his first try for the club. Three points behind and with the bit between their teeth, Vale rose in confidence and cancelled out all of Rochdale’s earlier advantages. The final word was delivered in the form of a relentless spell of Vale forward possession, well past 80 minutes, in the Rochdale 22. The ball was moved out to McGarvey, who then finished under the posts. Amidst the visiting crowd’s jubilation, Mayall - sporting a head bandage - kicked the conversion for Vale, whose first home fixture of the season comes against Leek RUFC on Saturday (3pm). Replacements: Bradshaw, Taylor-Smith, Ryder, Briggs, Gould.

candidates.source_body_excerpt: Rochdale AFC Community Trust will hold its annual sleep out at the Crown Oil Arena on Friday 9 October 2026. The event has been renamed the Change Lives Sleep Out to raise funds for its Changing Lives programme. The Trust held its first Rochdale Sleep Out with Petrus on 29 August 2025. Together, the two organisations raised £7,875.52. The Trust used its share of the money to help establish Changing Lives, a programme run in partnership with Petrus Housing for people experiencing homelessness or living in supported accommodation. The Trust says Changing Lives has supported 33 people in its first eight months. It offers free football alongside wellbeing, personal development and employability activities. Its aim is to give participants a place to meet others, improve their physical and mental wellbeing, and find routes into volunteering, education or work. During those eight months, the programme has held 28 football and engagement sessions, five specialist workshops and four free haircut sessions. Participants have played two competitive football fixtures and attended two Rochdale AFC first-team matches. When the partnership was announced in December 2025, Scott Webster, the Trust’s deputy director, said it would give people “the chance to improve their health and well-being, develop a sense of community and belonging, and gain valuable skills for future progression.” This year’s sleep out invites individuals, families, businesses, schools and community groups to spend a night under the floodlights at the Crown Oil Arena. People can join on their own or as part of a group. Those unable to take part can donate. The Trust says the event is intended to support people affected by homelessness, rather than recreate their experience. Money raised will help continue Changing Lives and offer its activities to more people. People can sign up or donate through the event page .

candidates.source_body_excerpt: Rochdale manager Ian Watson believes his side showed their mettle in the 2-1 win at Fleetwood. Goals from Dajaune Brown and Aden Flint put Dale 2-0 up early on but they were forced into sterling rearguard action in the second half, especially after Tobi Adebayo-Rowling saw a second yellow card 21 minutes from time, with Mark Helm having reduced the deficit. Watson, who had come under fire during Dale’s slow start to the season, said: “That’s what we want to look like all the time. “I’m just really pleased we get to see what we’re actually working on, what we’re trying to look like, and how brave the boys were with the ball, how much courage they played with. “When they do that, it’s really hard for the opposition. I felt the first 20 was really pleasing, then I think we maybe played the scoreboard a little bit after that and self-preservation mode kicked in a little bit. “We got to half-time and I thought we regrouped, and started the second half really well. There’s so much I love about today’s performance, not just with the ball, but everything without the ball, and the heart and desire the boys showed as well. “I understand where the frustration comes from but my responsibility is to not listen to any noise, just focus and back myself as a coach, as a human as well. My mentality is strong and I believe in myself. But how amazing were the fans as well, they got us over the line.” Fleetwood manager Matt Lawlor cut a frustrated figure having seen his side start slowly and then fail to break Dale down for an equaliser.

candidates.source_body_excerpt: Ten-man Rochdale survived a Fleetwood onslaught to earn a 2-1 victory at Highbury. The visitors raced into a two-goal lead inside 14 minutes, Dajaune Brown netting with a first-time finish from Glenn Middleton’s cross in the eighth minute before Aden Flint doubled Dale’s advantage, coolly slotting home after Brown’s shot fell kindly into his path. Mark Helm hit back on the half-hour mark, pouncing on a loose ball in midfield and finishing neatly into the bottom corner. Fleetwood pushed hard for an equaliser, with Ched Evans’ shot deflected inches wide, Raffaele Cirino hitting the side-netting and Aaron Loupalo-Bi narrowly wide with a fierce low drive. The home side dominated the second half but Lewis McCann clearing the bar by inches was as close as they got. Dale’s task got even tougher on 69 minutes when Tobi Adebayo-Rowling received a second yellow card for a shirt pull. Goalkeeper Sam Waller then denied Evans and Flint got his head to Ronan Coughlan’s goalbound shot as valiant defending, and Fleetwood’s wayward finishing, saw Dale hold on for the win.

candidates.source_body_excerpt: A Middleton woman who stopped drinking in 2019 says writing horror stories has helped her explore her experiences of addiction and trauma. Alex Herod said she tried meetings, therapy, books and sober communities before she began writing fiction as part of her recovery. She has a diagnosis of complex PTSD and is now working on a creative writing PhD about the role horror writing plays in her own recovery. “Although I write fiction, most of my stories relate back to themes of addiction, trauma, mental health, transformation and recovery,” she said. “Writing horror has allowed me to go into very dark places and come out the other side. I can explore feelings of disgust and monstrousness - how I felt about myself when I was drinking, or how I felt others saw me - and do so in a way that is in my control.” Alex said being able to edit and rewrite a story gives her a way to express experiences she previously felt unable to discuss. She described the process as “making friends with my monsters”. “It helps me to process my experiences of addiction and trauma, and learn to accept and embrace the darker parts of myself so I don’t feel disconnected,” she said. Alex, who works at the University of Salford, is due to release her debut novel next year. Goals from Dajaune Brown and Aden Flint put Dale 2-0 up early on but they were forced into sterling rearguard action in the second half, especially after Tobi Adebayo-Rowling saw a second yellow card 21 minutes from time, with Mark Helm having reduced the deficit. Watson, who had come under fire during Dale’s slow start to the season, said: “That’s what we want to look like all the time. “I’m just really pleased we get to see what we’re actually working on, what we’re trying to look like, and how brave the boys were with the ball, how much courage they played with. “When they do that, it’s really hard for the opposition. I felt the first 20 was really pleasing, then I think we maybe played the scoreboard a little bit after that and self-preservation mode kicked in a little bit. “We got to half-time and I thought we regrouped, and started the second half really well. There’s so much I love about today’s performance, not just with the ball, but everything without the ball, and the heart and desire the boys showed as well. “I understand where the frustration comes from but my responsibility is to not listen to any noise, just focus and back myself as a coach, as a human as well. My mentality is strong and I believe in myself. But how amazing were the fans as well, they got us over the line.” Fleetwood manager Matt Lawlor cut a frustrated figure having seen his side start slowly and then fail to break Dale down for an equaliser.

candidates.source_body_excerpt: Ten-man Rochdale survived a Fleetwood onslaught to earn a 2-1 victory at Highbury. The visitors raced into a two-goal lead inside 14 minutes, Dajaune Brown netting with a first-time finish from Glenn Middleton’s cross in the eighth minute before Aden Flint doubled Dale’s advantage, coolly slotting home after Brown’s shot fell kindly into his path. Mark Helm hit back on the half-hour mark, pouncing on a loose ball in midfield and finishing neatly into the bottom corner. Fleetwood pushed hard for an equaliser, with Ched Evans’ shot deflected inches wide, Raffaele Cirino hitting the side-netting and Aaron Loupalo-Bi narrowly wide with a fierce low drive. The home side dominated the second half but Lewis McCann clearing the bar by inches was as close as they got. Dale’s task got even tougher on 69 minutes when Tobi Adebayo-Rowling received a second yellow card for a shirt pull. Goalkeeper Sam Waller then denied Evans and Flint got his head to Ronan Coughlan’s goalbound shot as valiant defending, and Fleetwood’s wayward finishing, saw Dale hold on for the win.

At around 1.30am, Greater Manchester Police officers responded to reports of an assault in South Parade in Rochdale, where a man, aged 52, was found unconscious. He was taken to hospital for treatment but, despite the best efforts of emergency services, he sadly died. Two men have been arrested in connection with the incident and remain in custody for questioning. Detectives from the Major Incident Team are now leading the investigation and are appealing for anyone who witnessed the incident, has information about what happened, or has relevant CCTV, mobile phone or dashcam footage to come forward. The victim’s family are being supported by specialist officers. Detective Chief Inspector Claire Brennan, from the Major Incident Team, said : “This is a heart-breaking incident in which a man has tragically lost his life. “Our thoughts are first and foremost with his family and loved ones who are being supported by specially trained officers at this incredibly difficult time.

candidates.source_body_excerpt: Rochdale secured a 2-1 victory over Fleetwood Town at Highbury Stadium on September 26, 2026, despite playing the final 21 minutes with ten men following Tobi Adebayo-Rowling's dismissal.Dajaune Brown opened the scoring for the visiting side in the eighth minute with a right-footed finish from the center of the penalty area. Aden Flint doubled Rochdale's advantage six minutes later, striking into the bottom-left corner after Brown blocked an initial effort.Mark Helm brought Fleetwood Town back into the contest in the 30th minute. The midfielder received a pass from Aaron Loupalo-Bi outside the box and drove a right-footed shot into the bottom-right corner of the net.Fleetwood Town pushed for an equalizer before the break, but Rochdale goalkeeper Sam Waller maintained the visitors' lead by saving a header from captain Ched Evans and a tight-angle effort from Raff Cirino.Rochdale was reduced to ten players in the 69th minute when Adebayo-Rowling received a second yellow card for a foul on Loupalo-Bi. Fleetwood Town capitalized on the numerical advantage to create multiple opportunities in the closing stages.Waller made several key saves during the second half to deny Evans, Ronan Coughlan, and Lewis McCann. Fleetwood Town was unable to find a second goal despite five minutes of added time.Fleetwood Town manager Matt Lawlor adjusted his squad during the match, introducing Jake Batty for Kayden Hughes in the 64th minute and Coughlan for Adam Murphy in the 70th minute.

Ten-man Rochdale survived a Fleetwood onslaught to earn a 2-1 victory at Highbury.

The visitors raced into a two-goal lead inside 14 minutes, Dajaune Brown netting with a first-time finish from Glenn Middleton's cross in the eighth minute before Aden Flint doubled Dale's advantage, coolly slotting home after Brown's shot fell kindly into his path.

Mark Helm hit back on the half-hour mark, pouncing on a loose ball in midfield and finishing neatly into the bottom corner.

Dale's task got even tougher on 69 minutes when Tobi Adebayo-Rowling received a second yellow card for a shirt pull.

candidates.source_body_excerpt: Libraries across the borough are teaming up with a local charity to help families make use of thousands of free pre-loved school uniforms and shoes. As families continue to manage the high costs of school uniform, there is growing demand for affordable alternatives, including a reliance on local charities like Uniform For All, which Rochdale Council is working with to support those who need extra help. Every day high-quality pre-loved items, including polo shirts, skirts, trousers, branded school blazers, coats and pumps, are given to families through the charity. Not every family has the resources to travel long distances to collect their orders and the borough’s library service is helping to collect these items so families can pick them up closer to where they live at their nearest library and save on additional travel costs. When residents come in to collect their orders, library staff are also on hand to provide them with additional cost-of-living information and related support, if they need it, alongside free wifi and computer access and other benefits linked to a free library membership. Cllr Sue Smith, cabinet member for communities and co-operation, said: “We are proud to be supporting this valuable charity in distributing much-needed uniforms to our local families. “Sadly, we know demand is growing for these items so by utilising our libraries, we can help families access what they need within their communities.” Operating since 2020, Uniform For All currently provides more than 20,000 items to more than 3,000 families each year.

The evening had a waiting list, and we broadcast it live on Roch Valley Radio and across our social media platforms with a special video stream. Opening the ceremony, our chief executive and news editor David Murphy said Heywood Civic was a fitting place to hold the event after reopening earlier this year. He spoke about the people behind the awards and the role he wants our station to play in telling their stories. “Today, more than 120 people volunteer with Roch Valley Radio. They give their time, energy, ideas and experience to an organisation built around the rather unfashionable idea that having a platform is much more interesting when you use it to promote somebody other than yourself. “We have microphones, listeners, social media and the ability to make people pay attention. candidates.source_body_excerpt: A Greater Manchester Police operation aimed at protecting vulnerable young people has recorded 566 disruptions and generated more than 400 safeguarding referrals since it began in January 2024. Operation Luka involves police and partner agencies working to identify children at risk and target people suspected of exploiting them. GMP said the operation had recorded 566 disruptions by September 2026, which it described as the highest number recorded by one of its safeguarding operations. During deployments over the summer, teams engaged with 121 children, completed 12 care plans and visited 66 hotels of interest. Eleven arrests were also made through linked investigations. Operation Luka was launched in January 2024 and involves GMP's Complex Safeguarding Hub and partner organisations including children's services. Teams increased proactive patrols during the summer and have been working with young people in Manchester city centre. Mayor of Greater Manchester Bev Craig joined officers during a deployment in Piccadilly Gardens on Thursday 24 September.

candidates.source_body_excerpt: Police vans, restricted ticket sales and a week of winding each other up on social media. Sounds like Manchester United vs Manchester City, doesn’t it? Only this was Rochdale vs Oldham in League Two, with just seven miles separating the two towns. Six days after 74,161 fans watched the Manchester derby at Old Trafford, 6,121 packed into Spotland, including almost 2,000 travelling Oldham supporters. And for atmosphere, the fourth tier of English football certainly didn’t disappoint. A 12.30pm kick-off isn’t going to stop football fans getting to the pub early. By 10.30am, Rochdale town centre feels more like 6pm on a Saturday evening. Police vans separate the two sets of supporters, who’ve settled into different pubs and are busy winding each other up from behind the cordons. Dressed head to toe in Stone Island and C.P. Company, they’re taking turns telling each other exactly what they think of the other’s town. Most people, though, are simply going about their Saturday. A few confused shoppers look on as the town fills with football fans.

candidates.source_body_excerpt: This week's faith news from the Rochdale area You may have noticed scaffolding popping up around St M’s as we prepare for some building work on our roof, but we’re open as usual! Women’s breakfast returns from our summer break this morning, 9am until 10.30am. Breakfast butties, fellowship, and a short gospel talk. This year we’ve been thinking about the Ten Commandments and what they mean in our modern world. Today’s thought will cover ‘honouring your mother and father’. All ladies welcome, we'd love to meet you. No sign-up, no commitment, just turn up — maybe we'll see you there. Our Holy Communion service tomorrow starts at our usual time of 10.30am. Our sermon will be looking at Matthew chapter 8 verse 18 to chapter 9 verse 8. Children’s groups are available for ages 4–11. Join us after the service for cake and a brew. New here? We know walking into a new place can be scary, but we'll look after you. We would love to say hi during brew time and help you get connected into church life. Insight, formerly known as Youth Bible Study, meets on Sunday afternoon. The group made up of teens, in Years 10–13, from our three churches meets at Christ Church in Chadderton. This is a chance for young people to learn more about what the Bible actually says, and to meet people their own age. Parents, please contact vicar Rev Ben Wilkinson (vicar.balderstone@gmail.com) to register young people or for more information.
